sources.entry: Copy 2FA - Copies the newest 2FA code from Mail or Messages with one shortcut, and includes a Touch ID authenticator for TOTP and HOTP codes.

summary.one_liner: Copy 2FA is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that copies the newest verification code from Apple Mail or Messages with one keyboard shortcut and includes a Touch ID-protected authenticator for TOTP and HOTP codes.
summary.what_it_does: Pressing the global shortcut (default ⌃⇧C) finds the most recent verification code in Apple Mail or Messages and copies it to the clipboard, and it can show the last five codes from the past 10 minutes to choose from. A separate shortcut (⌃⇧A) opens a built-in authenticator that generates time-based (TOTP) and counter-based (HOTP) codes, with secrets stored in the keychain behind Touch ID. Accounts can be imported from several authenticator and password apps, from rsc/2fa, or from QR code screenshots. Each copied code shows its source, such as the sender and whether it came from Mail or Messages. The README says the app runs in the macOS App Sandbox without network access, reads only when a shortcut is pressed, and does not save what it reads.
use_cases: Copy a 2FA code from email to paste into a login page
Grab a texted bank or Duo verification code quickly
Generate TOTP or HOTP codes without a phone app
Migrate accounts from Google Authenticator, 1Password or Bitwarden
Pick an older verification code from recent messages
Avoid searching through email and texts for login codes
how_to_run: Download Copy-2FA.zip from the project's releases, unzip it, and move Copy 2FA to Applications
Open the app and allow Mail access when asked
Press ⌃⇧C when a code arrives to copy it
Build from source: git clone the repository and cd into copy-2fa
notable: Reads Apple Mail and Messages on a shortcut press, with no network entitlement enforced by the sandbox
Built-in authenticator supports TOTP and HOTP with Touch ID-protected keychain storage
Imports accounts from Google Authenticator, Apple Passwords, 1Password, Bitwarden, Aegis, 2FAS, andOTP, rsc/2fa and QR screenshots
Recent Codes menu lists the last five codes with their source
Has a Windows preview that reads Outlook and Thunderbird, per the README
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later; Messages access needs Full Disk Access turned on manually
Not notarized, so macOS shows a security warning on first launch and users must allow it in System Settings
Authy does not allow exports, so those accounts must be set up again; Duo push approvals cannot be read
Windows version is only a preview
